title: Quiz 7 Review – Heaps & Hashing
notes: Heap (general): A tree-based structure that is nearly complete and satisfies the heap-order property.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Binary heap: A heap where each node has at most two children and maintains heap-order.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Max-heap property: Every node’s key is ≥ the keys of its children; the maximum is at the root.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Min-heap property: Every node’s key is ≤ the keys of its children; the minimum is at the root.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Nearly complete tree: All levels are full except possibly the last, which is filled from left to right.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Heap height: For n items, the height is ⌊log₂ n⌋.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Array representation (0-index): Store nodes level-order in an array: parent(i)=⌊(i−1)/2⌋, left(i)=2i+1, right(i)=2i+2.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Array representation (1-index): Store nodes level-order in an array: parent(i)=⌊i/2⌋, left(i)=2i, right(i)=2i+1.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Sift-down (heapify-down): Restore heap by swapping a node with its best child until the property holds.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Sift-up (heapify-up): Restore heap by bubbling a node toward the root until the property holds.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Build-heap (Floyd’s method): Convert an array to a heap in O(n) by sifting down from ⌊n/2⌋ to 0.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Insert (heap): Place new item at end and sift-up; runs in O(log n).
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Extract-root (heap): Remove root, move last element to root, then sift-down; O(log n).
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Peek (heap): Read the root (min or max) in O(1) time.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Heapsort (idea): Build a heap then repeatedly extract the root to sort; in-place O(n log n), not stable.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Priority queue ADT: Abstract data type supporting insert, find-min/max, extract-min/max, and key updates.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Decrease-key / Increase-key: Adjust a key then sift-up (decrease in min-heap) or sift-down (increase in min-heap).
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Array-to-heap idea: Interpret array as level-order tree and apply bottom-up build-heap.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Heap-to-array idea: A heap stored in an array already represents level-order; reading array gives level-order traversal.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
d-ary heap: A heap where each node has d children, reducing height to O(log_d n).
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Meld support (binary heap): Binary heaps do not support fast meld; binomial/Fibonacci heaps do.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Cache friendliness (heap): Array layout is contiguous, aiding cache locality.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Hash table (definition): Maps keys to buckets using a hash function for fast average-time operations.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Hash function: Computes an integer hash value in [0, m−1] for table size m.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Bucket / Slot: A location indexed by the hash; may hold one or multiple keys depending on method.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Load factor (α): n/m where n is number of keys and m is number of buckets.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Collision: When two different keys hash to the same bucket.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Separate chaining: Resolve collisions by storing per-bucket lists/arrays of keys.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Open addressing: Resolve collisions by probing alternative buckets, storing all keys in the table array.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Probe sequence: Deterministic order of buckets tried in open addressing.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Linear probing: Probe i, i+1, i+2,…; simple but causes primary clustering.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Quadratic probing: Probe i + c1·k + c2·k²; reduces primary but may have secondary clustering.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Double hashing: Next probe uses a second hash h2 so index = h1 + k·h2 mod m.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Tombstone (hashing): Marker for a deleted slot so searches can continue along probe sequences.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Rehashing: Resize the table and reinsert all keys when α exceeds a threshold.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Modulo hashing: h(k)=k mod m; choose m carefully (often prime) to avoid patterns.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Multiplicative hashing: Use fractional part of k·A (0<A<1) scaled by m to spread keys.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Universal hashing: Pick a function at random from a family to limit expected collisions.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Perfect hashing: Two-level scheme for static sets giving O(1) worst-case lookups.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Cuckoo hashing: Use two locations; collisions evict existing keys, possibly triggering reinsertions.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Bloom filter: Probabilistic set with multiple hashes allowing false positives but no false negatives.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Expected search time: With controlled α and uniform hashing, expected O(1) for search/insert/delete.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf
Birthday paradox (intuition): Collisions become likely once n is on the order of √m.
Week 7 - Transform and Conquer; Space and Time Trade-offs.pdf

games.prompt: Match each term to its correct definition.
pairs: Heap (general)
A tree-based structure that is nearly complete and satisfies the heap-order property.
Binary heap
A heap where each node has at most two children and maintains heap-order.
Max-heap property
Every node’s key is ≥ the keys of its children; the maximum is at the root.
Min-heap property
Every node’s key is ≤ the keys of its children; the minimum is at the root.
Nearly complete tree
All levels are full except possibly the last, which is filled from left to right.
Heap height
For n items, the height is ⌊log₂ n⌋.
Array representation (0-index)
Store nodes level-order in an array: parent(i)=⌊(i−1)/2⌋, left(i)=2i+1, right(i)=2i+2.
Array representation (1-index)
Store nodes level-order in an array: parent(i)=⌊i/2⌋, left(i)=2i, right(i)=2i+1.
Sift-down (heapify-down)
Restore heap by swapping a node with its best child until the property holds.
Sift-up (heapify-up)
Restore heap by bubbling a node toward the root until the property holds.
Build-heap (Floyd’s method)
Convert an array to a heap in O(n) by sifting down from ⌊n/2⌋ to 0.
Insert (heap)
Place new item at end and sift-up; runs in O(log n).
Extract-root (heap)
Remove root, move last element to root, then sift-down; O(log n).
Peek (heap)
Read the root (min or max) in O(1) time.
Heapsort (idea)
Build a heap then repeatedly extract the root to sort; in-place O(n log n), not stable.
